about: Hand-written meta descriptions for pages whose opening text has no whole sentence short enough to be one. Shaped { lessons: {topic: text}, notes: {topic: text}, units: {chapter: text}, titles: {topic: text} }; "titles" is a shorter topic name for the <title> of its lesson and notes pages when the full one would be cut (two cut titles read the same). Never use the mark here: no "AP" in any meta description (docs/apcalc-spec.md decision 2).

notes.area-between-curves-x: The area between two curves is the integral of top minus bottom. How to find the limits, split the region where the curves cross, and check signs.
notes.area-between-curves-y: When the region's sides are curves x = f(y), slice it horizontally: integrate right minus left with respect to y. When to switch, and how to set it up.
notes.continuity-at-a-point: A function is continuous at x = c when f(c) is defined, the limit exists, and the two are equal. Each condition, how it fails, and how to justify continuity.
notes.cross-sections-triangles: Volumes of solids whose cross sections are triangles or semicircles: find the area A(x) of one slice from the base, then integrate it across the base.
notes.disc-method-other-axes: The disc method about a line such as y = 3 or x = −1: the radius is the distance from the curve to that line. How to set up and check the integral.
notes.infinite-limits: Infinite limits and vertical asymptotes: when a function grows without bound near a point, how to find the sign on each side, and how to write the limit.
notes.lhospitals-rule: L'Hospital's rule for limits of the form 0/0 or ∞/∞: check the form first, then take the limit of the quotient of derivatives. Worked examples and traps.
notes.limit-notation: What a limit is: the value f(x) closes in on as x approaches a number. How to read and write limit notation, including one-sided limits, with examples.
